passages.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor, just as it was with you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
Paul calls them brothers.
Paul asks them to pray for him and his companions.
Paul wants the word of the Lord to spread quickly.
Paul wants the word of the Lord to be honored.
Paul says the word of the Lord was honored among the Thessalonians.
passages.original: Τὸ λοιπὸν προσεύχεσθε ἀδελφοί περὶ ἡμῶν ἵνα ὁ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου τρέχῃ καὶ δοξάζηται καθὼς καὶ πρὸς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men; for not everyone holds to the faith.
passages.sermon: Some people are wicked and evil.\r\nSome people do not have faith.\r\nPray that God will deliver us from wicked and evil people.
passages.original: καὶ ἵνα ῥυσθῶμεν ἀπὸ τῶν ἀτόπων καὶ πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων οὐ γὰρ πάντων ἡ πίστις

passages.text: But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
passages.sermon: The Lord is faithful.\r\nThe Lord will strengthen you.\r\nThe Lord will guard you from the evil one.
passages.original: Πιστὸς δέ ἐστιν ὁ Κύριος ὃς στηρίξει ὑμᾶς καὶ φυλάξει ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ

passages.text: And we have confidence in the Lord that you are doing and will continue to do what we command.
passages.sermon:
We trust in the Lord.
We trust in the Lord concerning you.
You do what we command.
You will continue to do what we command.
passages.original: πεποίθαμεν δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἃ παραγγέλλομεν καὶ ποιεῖτε καὶ ποιήσετε

passages.text: May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is faithful.
The Lord guides His people.
The Lord directs your hearts.
He leads you into the love of God.
He leads you into the perseverance of Christ.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Κύριος κατευθύναι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας εἰς τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ εἰς τὴν ὑπομονὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life that is not in keeping with the tradition you received from us.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
Paul and his companions are leaders and teachers of the church.
Paul addresses the believers as brothers.
Paul gives a command.
Paul gives this command in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul tells the believers to keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life.
An undisciplined life means not following the teachings and example given by Paul and his companions.
Paul says the believers received a tradition from him and his companions.
Paul commands the believers to avoid anyone who does not live according to this tradition.
passages.original: Παραγγέλλομεν δὲ ὑμῖν ἀδελφοί ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ στέλλεσθαι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἀδελφοῦ ἀτάκτως περιπατοῦντος καὶ μὴ κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ἣν παρελάβοσαν παρ’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us, because we were not undisciplined among you, nor did we eat anyone’s food without paying for it. Instead, in labor and toil, we worked night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
passages.sermon:
You know how you should imitate us.
We did not live undisciplined lives among you.
We did not eat anyone’s food without paying for it.
We worked hard and labored.
We worked night and day.
We did this so we would not be a burden to any of you.
passages.original: αὐτοὶ γὰρ οἴδατε πῶς δεῖ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς ὅτι οὐκ ἠτακτήσαμεν ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδὲ δωρεὰν ἄρτον ἐφάγομεν παρά τινος ἀλλ’ ἐν κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἐπιβαρῆσαί τινα ὑμῶν

passages.text: Not that we lack this right, but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate.
passages.sermon:
We do not lack the right to receive support from you.
We chose not to use this right.
We wanted to give you an example.
We wanted you to imitate us.
passages.original: οὐχ ὅτι οὐκ ἔχομεν ἐξουσίαν ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἑαυτοὺς τύπον δῶμεν ὑμῖν εἰς τὸ μιμεῖσθαι ἡμᾶς

passages.text: For even while we were with you, we gave you this command: “If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat.”
passages.sermon: We were with you before.\r\nWe gave you a command at that time.\r\nWe said this to you: “If anyone does not want to work, he must not eat.”
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ ὅτε ἦμεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦτο παρηγγέλλομεν ὑμῖν ὅτι Εἴ τις οὐ θέλει ἐργάζεσθαι μηδὲ ἐσθιέτω

passages.text: Yet we hear that some of you are leading undisciplined lives and accomplishing nothing but being busybodies.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Thessalonica.
Paul and his companions are the speakers.
Paul addresses the believers in the church.
Paul says, “We hear news about some people among you.”
Some people in your group live in an undisciplined way.
These people do not do any real work.
Instead, they act as busybodies.
They interfere in matters that do not concern them.
passages.original: Ἀκούομεν γάρ τινας περιπατοῦντας ἐν ὑμῖν ἀτάκτως μηδὲν ἐργαζομένους ἀλλὰ περιεργαζομένους

passages.text: We command and urge such people by our Lord Jesus Christ to begin working quietly to earn their own living.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks with authority from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul addresses people who do not work and act as busybodies.
Paul commands these people.
Paul urges these people.
Paul gives this command in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul tells them to work quietly.
Paul tells them to earn their own bread.
Paul tells them to eat what they have earned.
passages.original: τοῖς δὲ τοιούτοις παραγγέλλομεν καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν ἐν Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἵνα μετὰ ἡσυχίας ἐργαζόμενοι τὸν ἑαυτῶν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν

passages.text: But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Thessalonica.
He calls them brothers.
He tells them to keep doing good.
He tells them not to become tired of doing what is right.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δέ ἀδελφοί μὴ ἐγκακήσητε καλοποιοῦντες

passages.text: Take note of anyone who does not obey the instructions we have given in this letter. Do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church.
Paul gave instructions in this letter.
Some people may not obey these instructions.
If someone does not obey, take note of that person.
Do not associate with that person.
This will help him feel ashamed.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις οὐχ ὑπακούει τῷ λόγῳ ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς τοῦτον σημειοῦσθε μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι αὐτῷ ἵνα ἐντραπῇ

passages.text: Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
passages.sermon: Do not treat him as an enemy.\r\nWarn him as you would warn a brother.
passages.original: καὶ μὴ ὡς ἐχθρὸν ἡγεῖσθε ἀλλὰ νουθετεῖτε ὡς ἀδελφόν

passages.text: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with all of you.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the Lord of peace.
The Lord Himself can give you peace.
He can give you peace at all times.
He can give you peace in every way.
The Lord be with all of you.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Κύριος τῆς εἰρήνης δῴη ὑμῖν τὴν εἰρήνην διὰ παντὸς ἐν παντὶ τρόπῳ ὁ Κύριος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν

passages.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this greeting with his own hand.
This greeting shows it is truly from Paul.
Paul writes every letter in this way.
This is Paul's mark in all his letters.
passages.original: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου ὅ ἐστιν σημεῖον ἐν πάσῃ ἐπιστολῇ οὕτως γράφω

passages.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you.
passages.sermon: Jesus Christ is our Lord.\r\nJesus Christ gives grace.\r\nMay the grace of Jesus Christ be with all of you.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν
